questions.stem: What is the name given to the system that includes all living organisms and their physical surroundings?
choices: Ecosystem
Environment
Biosphere
Community
questions.solution: An ecosystem is the term used to describe the system that includes all living organisms and their physical surroundings. The environment refers to the surroundings but not the interacting system of organisms. The biosphere is the global sum of all ecosystems, and a community refers only to the living organisms in an area, not their physical surroundings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a biodegradable substance?
choices: Plastic bags
Glass bottles
Leaves
Metal cans
questions.solution: Leaves are an example of a biodegradable substance because they can be broken down by natural processes involving microorganisms. Plastic bags and metal cans do not break down easily in the environment, making them non-biodegradable. Glass bottles also resist natural decomposition, so they are not biodegradable.

questions.stem: What is the main reason for the decrease in ozone layer thickness?
choices: Deforestation
Use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)
Industrial pollution
Natural climate change
questions.solution: The main reason for the decrease in ozone layer thickness is the use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which release chlorine atoms that break down ozone molecules in the stratosphere. Deforestation and industrial pollution do not directly affect the ozone layer, and natural climate change is not a primary cause of ozone depletion.

questions.stem: If a pond is left without cleaning, what might happen to the ecosystem in the long run?
choices: It could become polluted and unhealthy

questions.stem: What is the process called when harmful chemicals accumulate at each trophic level of a food chain?
choices: Biological concentration
Biological accumulation
Biological magnification
Biological intensification
questions.solution: The correct term is biological magnification, which describes how harmful chemicals become more concentrated at each higher trophic level in a food chain. This occurs because these chemicals are not easily broken down and accumulate as they are passed from one organism to another. Biological concentration and accumulation refer to the presence of chemicals in an organism but not their increasing concentration across the food chain. Biological intensification is not a recognized scientific term for this process.

questions.stem: If a pesticide is not biodegradable, what is the most likely impact on humans who consume food from the top of the food chain?
choices: It will be completely broken down by the human digestive system
It will be absorbed by plants and passed on to lower trophic levels
It will accumulate in the human body
It will be excreted without harm
questions.solution: Non-biodegradable pesticides persist in the environment and are not easily broken down. As they move up the food chain, they accumulate in the tissues of organisms, especially those at higher trophic levels, such as humans.
